evidence.source: CUHK Humanum, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解 / formation and disputed interpretations
evidence.text: The entry analyzes ordinary 好 as 女 plus 子 and favors a mother–child affection interpretation because early 子 is child-shaped and smaller than 女. It also reports alternatives attributed to Duan Yucai (a woman's beauty) and Xu Kai and Chen Weizhan (affection between a man and woman). The entry explicitly says the cited early written examples do not directly attest the proposed mother–child sense. These are the database editor's analysis and source-attributed proposals, not direct proof of original motivation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 好

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 早期用例 / Shang name and possible homograph
evidence.text: The entry cites the Shang oracle-bone divination 《合集》154, 婦好娩, and bronze inscription 婦好盉 for the name 婦好. It reports a separate proposal attributed to Tang Lan and Zhang Zhenglang: in this name, 好 may be 女 with 子 phonetic, read as 子 and representing the Shang 子 lineage name, hence a homograph of ordinary 好. The evidence supports keeping the name-use analysis separate from the ordinary character's semantic formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 好

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: The entry reports that bronze inscriptions first show 好 meaning ‘good/beautiful’, citing 虘鐘: 用樂好賓; it also cites 杜伯盨: 好朋友 for ‘friendly’. It gives Warring States bamboo examples for ‘like’ (郭店《老子甲》32) and friendly relations (清華簡《繫年》39, 108). Its inspected text does not supply absolute dates for the named bronze vessels, so these establish source-attributed inscriptional examples and broad period categories rather than a precisely dated first occurrence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 好

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: graphic forms / variant and borrowing examples
evidence.text: The entry presents early forms as 女 plus 子, notes that component placement can vary, and says some Warring States bamboo forms use 丑 in place of 女. It also reports a phonetic loan for 孝 in 羌伯簋. The inspected page provides image links and counts but the images were not visually inspected here; the reported variants therefore do not establish a full sequence of graphic change.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 好

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂瀏覽 / component placement and variant status
evidence.text: The entry says early oracle-bone and bronze component placement was not fixed: 女 and 子 could be on either side without changing the character. It classifies the side-switched form as a variant, and records later forms and variants involving 丑. This editorial account supports positional variation; its list does not demonstrate a direct chronological ancestry among every listed form.
evidence.title: [A00883] 好 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: ShuoWen.org, digitized 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen entry defines 好 as 美 and analyzes it as 从女、子, with fanqie 呼皓切. Xu Kai's note interprets 子 as an honorific for a man and calls the graph associative. Duan Yucai reads 好 as originally referring to a woman and extended to beauty generally. These are historical lexicographic interpretations, not independent evidence for the original motivation or earliest sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「好」

evidence.source: University of Michigan, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction v1.1
evidence.text: The reconstruction table lists Standard Mandarin hǎo ‘good’ as Middle Chinese xawX and Old Chinese *qʰˤuʔ, and hào ‘love, like (verb)’ as xawH and *qʰˤuʔ-s. These are reconstructions of 好 in the two lexical uses; because the ordinary graph is analyzed as 女 plus 子, neither is a proposed component pronunciation or phonetic-component comparison.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.field: modern readings / Standard Chinese and Cantonese
evidence.text: The entry gives Standard Chinese hǎo in Hanyu Pinyin and Guangzhou–Hong Kong Cantonese hou2 in Jyutping for the ‘good’ reading. These are readings of the whole character; the entry's 女 plus 子 account proposes no phonetic component.
evidence.title: 好 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry presents 女 (‘woman’) plus 子 (‘child’) as an associative analysis and lists proposals including maternal affection, good fortune from children, a man–woman relationship, a woman's beauty, and a girl's demeanor. It also links the distinct Shang/W. Zhou and Shuowen seal categories. These summaries are secondary accounts and do not demonstrate a dated semantic chain.
evidence.title: 好 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The module labels its reconstructions as Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese and lists hǎo ‘good’ as xawX, *qʰˤuʔ and hào ‘love, like (verb)’ as xawH, *qʰˤuʔ-s. The suffixal relation is a morphological analysis for the paired lexical readings, not a claim about which meaning is chronologically oldest or about a sound component in the graph.
evidence.title: Module:zh/data/och-pron-BS/好 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Institute of History and Philology Museum, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 婦好 / Shang context and oracle-bone record
evidence.text: The museum account identifies Fu Hao as one of King Wu Ding's consorts, reports that her tomb was excavated in 1976, and says oracle-bone inscriptions include roughly one to two hundred records related to her. It quotes a divination about her childbirth. This independently supports the Shang name context, but does not settle whether 好 in the name is the same lexical graph as ordinary 好 or a phonetic name graph.
evidence.title: 商代的王后在忙什麼？──婦好，好不好，好在哪？

gaps: The CUHK entry favors mother–child affection based on the form and relative size of components, but it acknowledges that cited early examples do not directly attest that proposed sense. Alternative origin accounts remain unresolved.

The earliest securely described attestation in the inspected evidence is a Shang personal-name context, not an unambiguous ordinary lexical ‘good’ use. CUHK reports a bronze inscription use for ‘good/beautiful’ but does not provide an absolute date for that vessel in the inspected entry.
The sequence from Shang name use to ordinary meanings is not established. CUHK reports a distinct homograph/phonetic analysis for 婦好; the identity of its graph with ordinary 好 remains disputed.

The sources give selected meanings and broad inscription periods, not a complete dated semantic history. No ordering of ‘good’, ‘friendly’, ‘beautiful’, or ‘like’ is inferred from a modern dictionary gloss list.

Graphic variation is reported, including reversed 女/子 placement and some Warring States bamboo forms with 丑; the precise chronology, source exemplars, and possible scribal corruption have not been independently reconstructed from artifact images here.
Shuowen is a transmitted historical analysis. Its definition ‘美也’ does not by itself date the first ordinary sense or validate its proposed motivation.

No component is proposed as phonetic in the ordinary 女 + 子 analysis, so a phonetic-series comparison was not applicable. The separate surname proposal says 子 is phonetic in 婦好; the actual pronunciation and etymology of a depicted object is not at issue there.
The phonetic-loan claim for 孝 in 羌伯簋 is reported by CUHK; this research did not independently inspect the vessel image or establish the inscription's date.

The ordinary character's standard readings were checked, but no component pronunciation is compared because 女 and 子 are analyzed semantically in this graph. Baxter–Sagart readings concern whole 好 readings only.
The Xiaoxuetang rights page was opened, but the site landing and query pages did not expose a usable 好 record in this browser. No Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.

The Commons oracle and bronze files are modern vector redrawings based on cited database forms, not photographs of ancient inscriptions. The Commons oracle source page was inspected; direct image URL resolution through the browser failed.
The hanziyuan pages referenced by the Commons file could not be opened in the browser, so the precise original database images J26184 and B17049 were not independently reviewed.
The chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw page surfaced in search but was not opened for detailed evidence and is not used as an image asset.
The prior repository's described Shuowen page and historical claims are carried forward only where noted; the newly opened Shuowen.org page exposed no extractable text in this pass.
